labels.text: Renew Program for IOP/PSC and Mobile Phleb

notes.text: “Renew Program” should only be available when the Draw Status badge has the text “Program renewal available” below it.

When the user clicks the “Renew Program” overflow action, a side sheet will appear with a quickview of a subset of fields from the initial order page. We will carry over the previous program information to make it easier for the user since most of the details won’t need to be changed.

When it’s the last draw in a monitoring program that is being collected by Quest (PSC/IOP or Mobile Phlebotomy), the text “Program renewal available” will appear below the Draw Status badge. This will highlight to the user that the program will be completing soon to prompt renewal. The overflow menu should have the “Renew Program” action available, which would be the same functionality as renewing for a clinic order.
The “Renew MRD Program” sidesheet should function the same as currently outlined above for renewing the program or modifying the information.

Once the user clicks “Submit” and the side sheet closes, the following will occur:
Confirmation toast message will be displayed.
“Program Renewal Available” below the Draw Status will be removed since renewal was completed.
New program orders should now appear on the Orders tab and the patient’s profile.
The suggested draw schedule will automatically populate for the user using the last draw in the current series and the selected frequency. The user can any of the individual draws if needed.

The Business changed their minds and now want an update to the draw schedule. If the user changes the date for Draw 1, it should automatically update the subsequent draws based off the frequency and the new date. This will only apply to the first draw. If they make changes to any other draws, it won’t affect the others.

The user needs to make 2 selections in order to activate the “Submit” button: Diagnosis and Statement of Medical Necessity e-signature. They can adjust the pre-populated information (frequency, draw schedule or where the draw will be performed by) if needed, but these would be optional actions.

On the Success page once a user has successfully renewed a patient’s program, clicking the “Close” button should direct them back to the Monitoring To-Do’s tab.
The following should occur upon a successful submit:
“Program Renewal Available” below the Draw Status will be removed since renewal was completed.
New program orders should now appear on the Orders tab and the patient’s profile.

If the user selects “Modify Information” from the sidesheet quickview, they will be directed to the full ordering page with all the information pre-populated from the previous program as well as any additional selections made from the sidesheet.
This page will be more concise, focusing on MRD and program level fields. The following changes will display:
Title of the page will update to “Monitoring Program Renewal”
Only show the MRD test group → Remove all others
Show Monitoring test/code as read-only text
Remove the “Single Test” option under Monitoring Frequency
Remove “Save as Draft” button
Rest of the ordering workflow should function as normal.

If the user decides to cancel out of the renewal ordering full page instead of submitting, they will be directed back to the Monitoring To-Do’s tab. No change will be made to that particular draw for the patient.

notes.text: “Mark Scheduled and Renew” should only be available for the “Schedule and Renew” badge.

Once the user clicks “Submit” and the side sheet closes, the following will occur:
Confirmation toast message will be displayed.
Badge updates to “Draw Scheduled” with the corresponding overflow menu of actions.
If the “Date of Collection” was updated, this change needs to be reflected in the table and other tabs (if applicable).
New program orders should now appear on the Orders tab and the patient’s profile.

Once the user clicks “Submit” and the side sheet closes, the following will occur:
Confirmation toast message will be displayed.
Row for the patient will be removed from the table since the draw was canceled. The canceled draw should also be removed in other tabs (if applicable) and patient’s profile.
Tab count and table pagination should update.
New program orders for the renewal should now appear on the Orders tab, Monitoring To-Do’s (if within the next 30 days) and the patient’s profile.

Confirmation toast message will be displayed.
Row for the patient will be removed from the table since the draw was canceled. The canceled draw should also be removed in other tabs (if applicable) and patient’s profile.
Tab count and table pagination should update.
Since the program has completed without renewal, the patient will be listed under the “Show Completed Programs Ready for Renewal” checkbox.

On the full ordering page, searching for a diagnosis displays 30 results, which would take up a lot of space and require more scrolling in the sidesheet, due to the smaller size. Because of this, we should limit the search results to 10 in this quickview, so the whole card can fit without scrolling and to minimize the height.
The Business mentioned the diagnosis should most likely stay the same, so generally they wouldn’t have to look for something else, but good to build out for those users who happen to update it.

The Draw Preference field by default will be pre-selected with the “Mark the last draw as scheduled” option. When this is selected, there will be a nested field of “Date of Collection” which is pre-populated with the current scheduled date, which is found under the “Upcoming Draw” column in the table.
Because this schedules the last draw in the program, the date can be changed as long as it’s within one year from the program’s start date. Any days after should be disabled in the datepipcker.

When the user clicks “Continue”, the stepper will advance to Step 2, which is Renew Program. The first step will now have a checkmark in place of a number and since they selected to mark the last draw as scheduled, the date of collection (MM/DD/YYYY) should appear below the “Schedule Last Draw” title.
A back arrow will be added to the header, so the user can go back to the first step if needed.

When the user clicks “Continue”, the stepper will advance to Step 2, which is Renew Program. The first step will now have a checkmark in place of a number and since they selected to cancel the last draw, we will say “Cancel” below the “Schedule Last Draw” title.
A back arrow will be added to the header, so the user can go back to the first step if needed.

Once on the renewal step, the same flow will take place as defined previously under Schedule Last Draw and Renew Program.
The only change is the verbiage in the yellow alert message is updated to reflect the cancel action.
Any changes the user makes to the renew program section should be retained if they happen to toggle between the Yes/No options for the “Do you want to renew the MRD program for this patient?” field.

If the user selects to renew the program for the patient, then all the renewal fields will appear in card format to help segment the information as well as due to how the current Diagnosis component is built. The order of the fields should follow the hierarchy on the order page.
The buttons at the bottom will update, adding an additional button of “Modify Information” since it’s needed as part of the renewal flow.

The user needs to make 2 selections in order to activate the “Submit” button: Diagnosis and Statement of Medical Necessity e-signature. They can adjust the pre-populated information (frequency, draw schedule or where the draw will be performed by) if needed, but these would be optional actions.

When the user clicks “Mark Scheduled and Renew”, a side sheet will appear with the same fields from the Mark Scheduled and Renew flows as we need the user to indicate the last draw appointment was set up as well as prompt for renewal.
Since there can be a lot of fields, implemented a guided workflow to segment the information into steps, so they can focus on one action a time. First they will decide if they want to schedule the last draw or cancel, since the date can only be changed within one-year from the program’s start date. Then they move on to the renewal prompt, which is optional.
The suggested draw schedule will automatically populate for the user using the last draw in the current series and the selected frequency. The user can any of the individual draws if needed.

Once the user clicks “Submit” and the side sheet closes, the following will occur:
Confirmation toast message will be displayed.
Badge updates to “Draw Scheduled” with adding “Program renewal available” below it, to give visual indication on the table that renewing is available.
The overflow menu should have an option to renew.
If the “Date of Collection” was updated, this change needs to be reflected in the table and other tabs (if applicable).
If the user selects “No, don’t renew”, the “Submit” button will activate. The yellow alert message will remain on the page in the effort to subtly prompt the user to renew.

When the user selects to cancel the last draw:
The “Date of Collection” field will disappear from the screen, since it’s tied to the “Mark the last draw as scheduled” option.
The “Select reason for cancellation” field will now appear under the “Cancel the last draw” option. This is current functionality for canceling an order.
The “Continue” button will be disabled until a reason is selected by the user.
Due to feedback from Compliance, we can present the most recently used diagnosis, but the user has to make the selection themselves, instead of the system automatically selecting it for them.
